subject: She was probably a teenager
preview: What Mary's yes really cost her, told in order from Scripture.
linkText: Who Was Mary, the Mother of Jesus? The Woman God Chose to Carry His Son

blocks.text: She was probably a teenager.
No army. No title. No wealth.
Just a poor girl from a small town called Nazareth.
And an angel showed up and asked her to carry the Son of God.
We hear Mary's name every Christmas. But think about what her yes actually meant.
An unmarried, pregnant girl in a small town where everyone would count the months.
A fiance who could have walked away and been fully within his rights.
Whispers she would carry for the rest of her life.
She said yes anyway.
"Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word."
She said that before she had a single answer to how it would work or what it would cost her.
Here is what I want you to understand.
God did not need status or wealth for His biggest plan. He needed a willing heart.
Mary did not understand everything about her son.
When the shepherds came, Scripture says she "kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart."
At the temple, an old man named Simeon told her a sword would pierce through her own soul.
Years later, at a wedding in Cana, she pointed the servants to her son: "Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it."
And when she finally stood near the cross, she watched Simeon's word come true.
But the last picture Scripture gives us of Mary is not grief. It is a woman still praying with the believers.
This Christmas, when you hear her name, I hope you see the courage behind it.
